title: How Many Bishops to BEAT Magnus?
summary: Short video: Tony plays the Magnus bot with an army of bishops worth 39 points (13 bishops, the material value of a normal army) plus his king, vs Magnus's normal army, and wins the first game quickly by forming bishop batteries.
rules: White has a king plus 13 bishops (39 points of material, equal to a normal army's value); no other pieces.
Black (Magnus bot) has a normal army.
Normal chess rules; keep bishops on both colours (same-colour bishops alone can't mate).
win_condition: Checkmate the Magnus bot (won in game 1).

opponent.name: Magnus (chess.com Magnus bot)
opponent.avatar_description: cartoon Magnus Carlsen: short brown hair, big smile, grey hoodie

setup: Black: standard. White: king on e1 and 13 bishops on ranks 1-2 (thumbnail shows ranks 1-5 filled with bishops and caption '28 Bishops? No.' — exact squares not stated; inferred split across light and dark squares).
visual_fx: Thumbnail: board full of white bishops, Magnus cartoon
current_impl_issues: Impl (kingplus t=B, n=1) starts with king + 1 bishop and adds one per loss; video starts directly with king + 13 bishops (39 points) and won the first game.
Bishops should be split across both square colours.
evidence: web_fetch transcript 0:00 'start with 39 points worth of Bishops which is the same as the number of points of material that you start a regular chess game with'; 4:22 'check mate all right that ended a lot more quickly'. Thumbnail '28 Bishops? No.'
